title: Do Large Language Models Possess a Theory of Mind? A Comparative Evaluation Using the Strange Stories Paradigm
abstract: arXiv:2603.18007v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The study explores whether current Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit Theory of Mind (ToM) capabilities -- specifically, the ability to infer others' beliefs, intentions, and emotions from text. Given that LLMs are trained on language data without social embodiment or access to other manifestations of mental representations, their apparent social-cognitive reasoning raises key questions about the nature of their understanding. Are they capable of robust mental-state attribution indistinguishable from human ability in its output, or do their outputs merely reflect superficial pattern completion? To address this question, we tested five LLMs and compared their performance to that of human controls using an adapted version of a text-based tool widely used in human ToM research. translated_title: 大型语言模型是否具备心智理论？基于“奇怪故事”范式的比较评估
translated_abstract: 本研究探讨当前大型语言模型（LLMs）是否表现出心智理论能力——即从文本中推断他人信念、意图和情绪的能力。鉴于大型语言模型是在没有社会具身性、也无法接触心理表征其他表现形式的语言数据上训练的，其表面上的社会认知推理引发了一个关键问题：它们究竟能够进行稳健的心理状态归因，在输出上与人类能力难以区分，还是其输出仅仅反映了表层的模式补全？为了回答这一问题，我们测试了五个大型语言模型，并采用在人类心智理论研究中广泛使用的基于文本工具（“奇怪故事”范式）的改编版本，将其表现与人类对照组进行比较。该测试要求回答关于故事中人物信念、意图和情绪的问题。结果显示，两者之间存在表现差距……
tldr: 本研究改编人类心智理论研究中广泛使用的“奇怪故事”范式，对五个大型语言模型与人类对照组进行比较评估，发现LLMs在从文本推断他人信念、意图和情绪方面与人类存在表现差距。
en_tdlr: This study adapted the Strange Stories paradigm from human Theory of Mind research to compare five LLMs against human controls, revealing a performance gap between LLMs and humans in inferring beliefs, intentions, and emotions from text.
